title: Thermodynamic pairing order in the stripe regime of the square-lattice Hubbard model
statement: For the zero-temperature repulsive square-lattice Hubbard model with nearest-neighbor hopping t, on-site repulsion U, t'=0 and hole doping delta=1/6, determine whether superconducting pairing persists in the two-dimensional thermodynamic limit at U/t=10 and at U/t=15, the two stronger-coupling stripe cases studied by Roth et al. Treat the two parameter cases separately.
source_locator: SRC-PHYS-003 section IV.3; SRC-PHYS-004 model parameters and discussion; SRC-PHYS-005 pp. 2-3.
status_basis: Roth et al. explicitly leave persistence of stripe-phase pairing unresolved. Inspected 2026 claims use different doping or hopping parameters; no resolution of this exact target was found.
plain_summary: Electron stripes and superconducting pairing compete or coexist in the Hubbard model. Pairing on a finite cluster may disappear as both dimensions grow; the source leaves this limit unresolved.
assumptions: H=-t sum_<ij>,sigma (c†_i,sigma c_j,sigma+h.c.) +U sum_i n_i,up n_i,down on the square lattice; t>0, no next-nearest hopping, and delta=1-N_e/N_sites=1/6. Consider zero temperature and U/t=10 and 15 separately.
Specify lattice shape, boundaries and particle-number convention before comparing results.
The two-dimensional limit requires both linear dimensions to grow; a fixed-width cylinder has a different limit.
scope: Pairing in the source's strong-coupling stripe regime, not a complete phase diagram or a claim about every cuprate.
target: Determine whether long-range superconducting order survives, with controlled treatment of finite-size and method errors.
success_criteria: Specify a singlet-pair observable and long-range-order criterion, and assess its limit alongside stripe correlations. Explain how particle-number conservation and boundary pinning enter the estimator.
Report competing states and uncertainty from geometry, ansatz, optimization and sampling.
Identify numerical evidence as such; a rigorous theorem requires a separate proof.
known_results: SRC-PHYS-003 reports pairing in a 144-site stripe state and explicitly leaves the thermodynamic question open.
SRC-PHYS-004 reports later superconductivity evidence at delta=1/8, U/t=8, t'/t=-0.2; these parameters differ.
SRC-PHYS-005 makes broad resolution claims but uses U/t=6 and nonzero t'/t in the inspected setup.
prerequisites: Variational Monte Carlo or tensor-network methods
significance: Clarifying intertwined orders in a central interacting-electron model would improve theoretical understanding of correlated superconductivity.
